answer: Copying the same citations across 114 aliases hence pays the authoring cost 114 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the umber index resolves every citation against the juniper checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the sonnet audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 2 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. That is 12 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
